subject: Science
title: Rolling and sliding
objectives: Children will test objects to see which roll and which slide.
Children will roll a ball or car down a ramp.
content: Finding which things roll and which things slide, and rolling a ball or car down a ramp.
teachingActivities: Let children test objects freely; name each test result; use a ramp made from a board on a low box; keep the slope gentle; let children predict by pointing.
learnerActivities: Test objects to see which roll and which slide and roll a car down a ramp.
resources: A ball, a toy car, a block, a tin and a cup
assessment: Observe whether each child says roll or slide after trying and rolls a car down a ramp.
expectedOutcomes: Says roll or slide after trying.
Rolls a car down a ramp.

lessons.title: Things that roll
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will find things that roll.
successCriteria: Rolls a ball and a tin
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can push and pull objects and say the words.
resources: A ball, a tin and a toy wheel
lessons.starter: Roll a ball across the floor and say "Roll, roll, roll. The ball rolls."
teacherActivities: Roll the ball, the tin and the wheel one at a time and say "Roll."
Try to roll a block and see what happens.
Let each child roll an object.
Ask "What rolls?" and point to objects.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say roll.
Children watch it stop.
Child rolls an object and says roll.
Child points to rolling things.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Roll the ball, the tin and the wheel one at a time and say "Roll." Children: Children watch and say roll.
Step 2. Teacher: Try to roll a block and see what happens. Children: Children watch it stop.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child roll an object. Children: Child rolls an object and says roll.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What rolls?" and point to objects. Children: Child points to rolling things.

practical.title: Roll it
steps: Sit in a circle and roll objects to a friend.
practical.safety: Sit with legs apart and roll objects slowly. Use soft items and clear the floor of obstacles.

differentiation.support: Roll the ball together and watch it go.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another thing that rolls.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says roll for things that roll
lessons.conclusion: Roll the ball slowly to each child and say goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Roll different things at home and see which roll.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find things that roll" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Roll, roll, roll the ball. Roll, roll, roll.

lessons.title: Things that slide
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will find things that slide.
successCriteria: Slides an object on a smooth surface
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can push and pull objects and say the words.
resources: A block, a book and a cloth on a smooth tray
lessons.starter: Slide a block along the smooth board and say "Slide, slide, slide."
teacherActivities: Slide objects along a smooth surface and say "Slide."
Try a rough surface and see that it is harder to slide.
Let each child slide an object.
Go to the playground slide with an adult and slide down safely.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say slide.
Children watch and say stop.
Child slides an object.
Child slides down and says slide.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Slide objects along a smooth surface and say "Slide." Children: Children watch and say slide.
Step 2. Teacher: Try a rough surface and see that it is harder to slide. Children: Children watch and say stop.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child slide an object. Children: Child slides an object.
Step 4. Teacher: Go to the playground slide with an adult and slide down safely. Children: Child slides down and says slide.

practical.title: Slide it
steps: Put a smooth board on a table.
practical.safety: Supervise the playground slide closely and let children slide one at a time. Keep the board low and steady.

differentiation.support: Slide the object together and say slide.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find which surface is best for sliding.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the rough mat good for sliding?

expectedOutcomes: Says slide for things that slide
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say "Slide, slide."
lessons.homeConnection: Slide a toy on a smooth floor or table at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find things that slide" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Roll or slide?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will test objects and decide if they roll or slide.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can push and pull objects and say the words.
resources: Six objects: ball, tin, cup, block, book, toy car
Two hoops labelled roll and slide
lessons.starter: Show a tin and a block and ask "Which one will roll? Let us try."
teacherActivities: Hold up an object and ask for a guess.
Test the object on the floor.
Put the object in the roll or slide hoop.
learnerActivities: Children guess with a word or point.
Children watch and say roll or slide.
Child places the object in the right hoop.
Children say roll or slide for each object.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up an object and ask for a guess. Children: Children guess with a word or point.
Step 2. Teacher: Test the object on the floor. Children: Children watch and say roll or slide.
Step 3. Teacher: Put the object in the roll or slide hoop. Children: Child places the object in the right hoop.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each hoop together. Children: Children say roll or slide for each object.

practical.title: Test and sort
steps: Sort it into roll or slide hoops.
practical.safety: Use large objects only and keep the floor clear. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Offer two objects and test them together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a new object and test it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Sorts objects into roll and slide
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say "Roll and slide."
lessons.homeConnection: Test which things roll and which slide at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "test objects and decide if they roll or slide" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Ramp rolling
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will roll a ball or a car down a ramp.
successCriteria: Rolls a car down a ramp
Says fast or slow with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can push and pull objects and say the words.
resources: A smooth board ramp on a low box
A toy car and a ball
lessons.starter: Roll a ball down a ramp and say "Down the ramp it goes! Fast, fast."
teacherActivities: Set up a gentle ramp and roll a ball down.
Let each child roll a car down the ramp.
Make the ramp steeper and then flatter and see what changes.
Ask "Which is faster, the car or the block?"
learnerActivities: Children watch and say fast.
Child rolls the car and watches.
Children watch and say fast or slow.
Child points to the faster one.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up a gentle ramp and roll a ball down. Children: Children watch and say fast.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child roll a car down the ramp. Children: Child rolls the car and watches.
Step 3. Teacher: Make the ramp steeper and then flatter and see what changes. Children: Children watch and say fast or slow.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Which is faster, the car or the block?" Children: Child points to the faster one.

practical.title: Ramp race
practical.safety: Keep the ramp low and steady. Put a cone or a box at the end so objects do not roll away. Keep fingers out of the way.

differentiation.support: Roll the car together and watch it go.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to guess which toy will go the furthest.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Does the car go fast or slow?
What happens on a flat ramp?

expectedOutcomes: Rolls a car down a ramp
lessons.conclusion: Put the ramp away and say "Down, down, down."
lessons.homeConnection: Make a ramp with a book and roll a toy car down it.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "roll a ball or a car down a ramp" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 2 roll and slide check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child tests objects and uses roll and slide words.
successCriteria: Says roll or slide after trying
Rolls a car down a ramp
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can push and pull objects and say the words.
lessons.starter: Sing the roll and slide song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: roll, slide and ramp.
At each station ask "Roll or slide?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or action.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: roll, slide and ramp. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Roll or slide?" Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Roll and slide stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Keep ramps low.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one object.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain roll and slide to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says roll or slide; tests objects; rolls a car down a ramp.

questions.question: Can you roll it down the ramp?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye with a roll and a slide.
lessons.homeConnection: Roll and slide toys at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child tests objects and uses roll and slide words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
